questions.question: What is a stanza?
options: A group of lines forming a unit in a poem
The title of a poem
A type of rhyme
The last line of a sonnet
questions.explanation: A stanza is a group of lines forming a unit — the poetic equivalent of a paragraph.

questions.question: What is enjambment?
options: When a sentence continues from one line to the next without pause
A pause in the middle of a line
A rhyme at the end of a line
The repetition of a whole stanza
questions.explanation: Enjambment runs a sentence across the line break; a caesura is a pause in the middle of a line.

questions.question: What is metre in poetry?
options: The rhythmic pattern of stressed and unstressed syllables
The number of stanzas
The poem's physical length on the page
The poet's signature
questions.explanation: Metre is the rhythmic pattern of stressed and unstressed syllables, like iambic pentameter.

questions.question: Which are sound devices in poetry?
options: Rhyme, alliteration, assonance and onomatopoeia
Plot, setting and character
Margins, fonts and titles
Chapters, prefaces and indexes
questions.explanation: Sound devices — rhyme, alliteration, assonance, onomatopoeia — create the musical quality of poetry.

questions.question: What should poetry analysis always do?
options: Connect technique to meaning — explain why a device is used and its effect
Simply list every device found
Count the words in each line
Avoid interpreting the poem
questions.explanation: Strong analysis explains not just what device is used, but why and to what effect.
